newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn must learn from metal deal - German opposition.
newsitem.headline: Bonn must learn from metal deal - German opposition.

text.p: German parliamentary opposition leader Rudolf Scharping on Thursday said a surprise overnight deal that could solve a bitter pay dispute in the metal and engineering sector was a lesson to the Bonn government.
Union and employer negotiators in the northern state of Lower Saxony earlier signed a deal securing worker sick pay at full salary, spurning a new federal law allowing cuts in sick pay entitlements.

"Other (industries) should follow and the Bonn coalition, destroyer of social peace, should take note of the sense of responsibility (shown by the two sides)," Scharping, parliamentary leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) party, said in a statement.
All-out strikes in the industry had been widely expected next spring following the collapse of previous attempts to resolve the dispute.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government had in October introduced a law cutting sick payments to 80 percent of salary as part of austerity package designed to ensure entry into the single European currency in 1999.
Initial attempts by firms in the metal and engineering sector to implement the new law have however been met by protests involving hundreds of thousands of workers.

IG Metall officials said they were now optimistic that the deal reached in the relatively small Lower Saxony region could now be applied to larger areas, such as the steel-making region of North Rhine-Westphalia.

Employers in other industries have been more successful in imposing the cuts. Most of Germany's main banks have now reduced sick pay to 80 percent despite a growing wave of resentment among normally peaceable bank workers.
